title: NDP-MSH binding melanocortin-1 receptor ameliorates neuroinflammation and BBB disruption through CREB/Nr4a1/NF-κB pathway after intracerebral hemorrhage in mice

citation.title: NDP-MSH binding melanocortin-1 receptor ameliorates neuroinflammation and BBB disruption through CREB/Nr4a1/NF-κB pathway after intracerebral hemorrhage in mice

printed_heading.text: RESEARCH Open Access NDP-MSH binding melanocortin-1 receptor ameliorates neuroinflammation and BBB disruption through CREB/Nr4a1/NF-κB pathway after intracerebral hemorrhage in mice Xuan Wu1 , Siming Fu1 , Yun Liu1 , Hansheng Luo1 , Feng Li1 , Yiying Wang2 , Meng Gao2 , Yuan Cheng1 and Zongyi Xie1*

what_it_measured.text: This study aimed to investigate whether NDP-MSH could alleviate neuroinflammation and BBB disruption after experimental ICH, as well as the potential mechanisms of its neuroprotective roles.

dose.text: To evaluate the effects of NDP-MSH on neuroinflammation and BBB integrity, three doses of NDP-MSH (1.5, 5, 15 μg/mouse, Anaspec, USA) dissolved in phosphatebuffered saline (PBS) were administered intraperitoneally at 1 h after ICH insult.

To investigate the underlying mechanisms of NDP-MSHmediated neuroprotective effects, Nr4a1 siRNA was administered by i.c.v injection at 48 h before ICH induction, and then followed with NDP-MSH (5 μg/mouse) treatment at 1 h after ICH.

route.text: Experiment 2 To evaluate the effects of NDP-MSH on neuroinflammation and BBB integrity, three doses of NDP-MSH (1.5, 5, 15μg/mouse, Anaspec, USA) dissolved in phosphatebuffered saline (PBS) were administered intraperitoneally at 1h after ICH insult.

endpoint.text: Evans blue (EB) extravasation was evaluated at 24 h after ICH.
The time course of endogenous Mc1r in the perihematoma tissue was measured by Western blot.
Moreover, to validate the knockdown efficiency of Nr4a1 siRNA, the expression of Nr4a1 was measured by Western blot.

reported_results.text: Administration of NDP-MSH improved neurological deficits and reduced brain edema and BBB permeability after ICH The neurological deficits and brain edema were evidently worse at 24 and 72 h post-ICH in the ICH +vehicle and ICH +NDP-MSH (1.5 μg/mouse) groups, when compared with sham group.
Results Mortality and exclusion The total mortality of ICH mice was 9.34% (17/182) in this study.

Treatment with NDP-MSH significantly improved neurological deficits (a and b) and reduced brain water content (c) at 24 and 72 h, as well as decreased EB extravasation at 24 h after ICH (d). n = 6 for each group.
